title: The Schurman Commission
subtitle: Five men, five months, one report that shaped the next fifty years.
objectives: Explain who the Schurman Commission were and why they came
List the main recommendations of the report
Explain the claim that Filipinos were 'not ready'
Compare what was recommended with what actually happened
Explain why the school recommendation mattered most

cards.title: President McKinley sent five men to find out
cards.text: They arrived in March 1899, one month after the war began. They were told to investigate and to recommend.

cards.title: A university president in charge
cards.text: Jacob Gould Schurman ran Cornell University. Admiral Dewey and General Otis were already in Manila and joined him.
points: **Dewey and Otis**, the navy and the army.
**Dean Worcester**, a zoologist who knew the islands.

cards.title: Two of the five were fighting the people they were studying
cards.text: Dewey and Otis were commanders in the war going on around them. They were also asked to judge fairly.
points: **A commission is only as neutral** as the people on it.
**Nobody hid this.** It was normal at the time.
**Ask who wrote a source** before you trust it.
**That is a history skill**, not an insult.

question.text: What was the Schurman Commission asked to do?
options: Investigate conditions and recommend a policy
question.explain: It was advisory. It gathered evidence and wrote a report, and could not legislate.

cards.title: What they said, and what followed
cards.text: Tap each number. The second line is what actually happened afterwards.

cards.title: January 1900
cards.text: They interviewed Filipinos, Spaniards and Americans, and produced a report the American government then used for years.

cards.title: Pause here
cards.text: Part 2 looks hard at the 'not ready' claim. Come back when you are set.

cards.eyebrow: Part 2 · The claim at the centre
cards.title: 'Filipinos are not yet ready to govern themselves'
cards.text: This one sentence justified everything else in the report. It is worth testing against what was already happening.

cards.title: The republic already existed
cards.text: The Malolos Constitution had been in force since January 1899. There was a congress, a cabinet and a court system.
points: **All of it running** while the report was written.

cards.title: 'Not ready' is never a measurement
cards.text: A fighter is told he is not ready. Who decided, what was the test, and does that person gain if he waits?
points: **The people judging** were the people staying.
**Ask those three questions** of any 'not ready'.

question.text: There was no functioning Filipino government when the Commission called Filipinos unready.
question.explain: False. The Malolos Republic had a constitution, a congress and courts, all running at the time.

cards.title: Most of it did happen
cards.text: This is the awkward part. The civil government came, the legislature came, and the schools came.

cards.title: 'Eventually' with no date is not a promise
cards.text: A training plan says what you do and when it ends. A plan with no end date is not a plan.

question.text: Which recommendation had the biggest effect on ordinary Filipino life?
question.explain: Act No. 74 in 1901 built a free school system. It reached more people than any other change.

terms.def: The First Philippine Commission, 1899. Advisory only.
Its chairman, and president of Cornell University.
Able to recommend, not able to decide or make law.
The 1901 law that created the free public school system.
Independence promised with no date attached. It came in 1946.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Sent by McKinley in 1899**, reported in January 1900.
**'Not ready'** was a claim, not a measurement.
**Free public schools** was the recommendation that landed hardest.

quiz.text: Who sent the Schurman Commission to the Philippines?
quiz.explain: McKinley sent it in 1899 to investigate conditions and recommend a policy.
quiz.objective: Explain who the Schurman Commission were and why they came

quiz.explain: Schurman was president of Cornell University. The commission carries his name.
quiz.objective: Explain who the Schurman Commission were and why they came

quiz.text: Two members of the Commission were American commanders in the ongoing war.
quiz.explain: True. Admiral Dewey and General Otis were both serving commanders in the Philippines.
quiz.objective: Explain who the Schurman Commission were and why they came

quiz.text: What kind of power did the Commission have?
quiz.explain: It could investigate and recommend. The Taft Commission of 1900 got the law-making power.
quiz.objective: Explain who the Schurman Commission were and why they came

quiz.text: Which of these did the report recommend?
options: Replacing military rule with a civil government
quiz.explain: Civil government, a partly elected legislature, local autonomy and free public schools.
quiz.objective: List the main recommendations of the report

quiz.text: What did the report say about independence?
options: It should come eventually, but not yet
quiz.explain: Eventually, with no date attached. It arrived in 1946.
quiz.objective: List the main recommendations of the report

quiz.text: What reason did the Commission give for delaying independence?
options: That Filipinos were not yet ready to govern themselves
That Spain still had a legal claim
That Filipinos had asked for a delay
That the islands were too small
quiz.explain: That single claim justified the rest of the report.
quiz.objective: Explain the claim that Filipinos were 'not ready'

quiz.text: What is the strongest evidence against the 'not ready' claim?
options: The Malolos Republic already had a constitution, congress and courts
quiz.explain: The republic had been running since January 1899, while the report was being written.
quiz.objective: Explain the claim that Filipinos were 'not ready'

quiz.text: When was the civil government recommendation carried out?
quiz.explain: 4 July 1901, with Taft as the first Civil Governor.
quiz.objective: Compare what was recommended with what actually happened

quiz.text: How long after the report did independence actually arrive?
quiz.explain: The report was published in January 1900. Independence came on 4 July 1946.
quiz.objective: Compare what was recommended with what actually happened

quiz.text: Which law created the free public school system?
quiz.explain: Act No. 74, passed in 1901, set up free primary education across the islands.
quiz.objective: Explain why the school recommendation mattered most

quiz.text: The school recommendation reached more Filipinos than any other part of the report.
quiz.explain: True. Legislatures affected a small elite. Schools reached ordinary children everywhere.
quiz.objective: Explain why the school recommendation mattered most

teacher.summary: Week 9 follows the Term 1 scope on the Schurman Commission. The lesson does two things at once: it teaches the report's contents accurately, since that is what the exam asks for, and it models how to interrogate a source — who wrote it, what were they doing at the time, and what claim is doing the load-bearing work. The 'not ready' card is the centre. It is tested against a specific verifiable fact, the Malolos Republic's existence at the time, rather than against an opinion. The lesson also credits the schools recommendation honestly; the period is not made simpler by pretending nothing good came from it.
discussion: Ask what changes about a report when two of its five authors are commanding the war it studies.
Ask him to state the 'not ready' claim, then say what evidence would settle it either way.
Ask why 'eventually' with no date is different from a promise.
Ask which recommendation he would have argued hardest for, and why.
teacher.extension: Have him write the one-paragraph dissent a Filipino member of the Commission might have filed, if there had been one. There was not, which is itself worth noticing.
misconceptions: 'The Schurman Commission governed the Philippines.' It was advisory. Taft's commission held the legislative power.
'The report was ignored.' Most of it was implemented, some of it within two years.
'There was no Filipino government at the time.' The Malolos Republic was functioning while the report was written.
'Independence was promised for a set date.' No date was ever given. It came in 1946.
